subject: Biology
description: Fungi: structure, classification, reproduction, ecological roles, useful and harmful fungi, fungal diseases, edible vs poisonous, antibiotics from fungi.

questions.stem: Fungi are classified separately from plants because they:

options.option_text: Live only on decaying matter alone

questions.explanation: KEY DISTINCTION: fungi LACK CHLOROPHYLL → cannot make their own food via photosynthesis → they are HETEROTROPHS (consume organic matter from other organisms). Plants are AUTOTROPHS (chlorophyll-bearing, photosynthetic). FIVE-KINGDOM CLASSIFICATION (Whittaker, 1969) places fungi as a separate kingdom: Monera (bacteria), Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia. FUNGAL CELL WALLS: made of CHITIN (same polymer as insect exoskeletons!) — NOT cellulose like plants. NUTRITION MODES: (1) SAPROPHYTIC (decompose dead organic matter) — most fungi, e.g., mushrooms on logs; (2) PARASITIC (feed on living hosts) — e.g., wheat rust fungus, athlete's foot; (3) SYMBIOTIC — lichens (fungus + alga), mycorrhizae (fungus + plant roots, ~90% of land plants depend on this). ECOSYSTEM ROLE: fungi are PRIMARY DECOMPOSERS — without them, dead plant matter (lignin, cellulose) wouldn't break down, halting nutrient cycles. PYQ ANGLE: NCERT Class 11 Ch. 2 (Biological Classification) — high-yield for NEET, SSC.

questions.stem: Penicillin, the world's first antibiotic, is derived from a fungus called:
questions.explanation: PENICILLIN was discovered ACCIDENTALLY by Alexander Fleming in 1928 at St Mary's Hospital, London. He noticed a Penicillium notatum mould had contaminated a Petri dish of Staphylococcus bacteria — and a clear zone of bacterial death surrounded the mould. The compound was isolated and mass-produced by Howard Florey and Ernst Chain (Oxford, 1940s) — the trio shared the 1945 Nobel in Medicine. WW2 IMPACT: penicillin saved thousands of soldiers from bacterial infections — by 1944, US factories made enough for D-Day. MECHANISM: penicillin disrupts bacterial cell-wall synthesis (inhibits peptidoglycan cross-linking), killing bacteria but not human cells (we lack cell walls). MODERN VARIANT: Penicillium chrysogenum is the industrial strain — yields ~1000× more penicillin than original. RELATED FUNGI ANTIBIOTICS: Cephalosporins (Cephalosporium fungi); Griseofulvin (Penicillium griseofulvum, antifungal); Cyclosporine (Tolypocladium inflatum, immunosuppressant). PYQ ANGLE: SSC, NEET, RRB all repeatedly test penicillin discoverer + source — 90%+ frequency.

questions.stem: Yeast, used in bread-making and brewing, performs which type of respiration to release CO₂?
questions.explanation: YEAST (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) performs ANAEROBIC RESPIRATION (fermentation) in the absence of oxygen: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2 C₂H₅OH (ethanol) + 2 CO₂ + ~2 ATP. The CO₂ makes BREAD RISE; the ETHANOL is the basis of WINE, BEER, and SPIRITS production. AEROBIC ALTERNATIVE: with O₂, yeast respires fully like animals (glucose → CO₂ + H₂O + ~36 ATP). Used commercially in industrial yeast farming. INDUSTRIAL ETHANOL: India produces ~3 billion litres ethanol annually for E20 fuel-blending program (20% ethanol in petrol by 2025-26). HISTORY: yeast's role discovered by Pasteur (1857) — disproved 'spontaneous generation' theory of fermentation. BAKING: dough at 25-30°C lets yeast multiply and produce CO₂ bubbles; oven heat then kills yeast (>50°C) and bakes the bread. WINE: grape sugars → ethanol; ABV typically 12-15%; above 15% kills yeast. KOMBUCHA / KEFIR: also yeast-driven fermentations. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'yeast in bread' is a Class 8-10 NCERT staple — appears in CGL Tier 1 yearly.

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases is caused by a fungus?

options.option_text: Malaria is caused by a protozoan.
Influenza is caused by a virus.

questions.explanation: ATHLETE'S FOOT (tinea pedis) is caused by DERMATOPHYTE FUNGI (Trichophyton species). It thrives in warm, moist environments (gym showers, sweaty shoes). RELATED FUNGAL INFECTIONS: ringworm (tinea corporis — body), jock itch (tinea cruris — groin), nail fungus (onychomycosis), candidiasis/thrush (Candida albicans — mouth, vagina), aspergillosis (lung infection in immunocompromised). KEY DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS — common diseases by causative agent: BACTERIAL: TB, cholera, typhoid, leprosy, plague, tetanus; VIRAL: flu, COVID-19, dengue, chikungunya, HIV/AIDS, polio, measles, hepatitis-B; PROTOZOAN: malaria, amoebiasis, kala-azar, sleeping sickness; FUNGAL: athlete's foot, ringworm, candidiasis. INDIA HEALTH IMPACT: fungal infections affect ~25-40% population annually (largely tinea); over-the-counter clotrimazole/terbinafine creams treat most cases. RECENT EMERGENCE: Mucormycosis ('black fungus') surged during COVID-19 second wave (2021) in immunosuppressed patients. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'disease classification by causative agent' is a perennial CGL/Banking GA topic.

questions.stem: A LICHEN is a symbiotic association between:

options.option_text: A fungus and an alga (or cyanobacterium)
A fungus and a moss alone (option here)

questions.explanation: LICHEN = mutualism between FUNGUS (provides shelter, water-absorbing structure, mineral nutrients) and ALGA or CYANOBACTERIUM (provides food via photosynthesis). The fungal partner is typically Ascomycete; the photosynthetic partner is Trebouxia (green alga) or Nostoc (cyanobacterium). EXAMPLES: Cladonia (reindeer moss — Arctic), Usnea (old man's beard — temperate forests), Parmelia (rocks/walls — common in India). ECOLOGICAL ROLE: lichens are PIONEER ORGANISMS — first colonizers of bare rock; they secrete acids that slowly weather rock into soil over centuries. POLLUTION INDICATORS: lichens are HIGHLY SENSITIVE to SO₂ pollution; their absence in a city signals high air pollution. ('Industrial deserts' = lichen-free zones around coal-fired plants.) FOOD: some Tibetan/Lapland communities eat lichens (Cetraria islandica). MEDICINE: usnic acid from Usnea has antibacterial properties. INDIA: ~2300 lichen species recorded; Western Ghats and Himalayas are biodiversity hotspots. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests symbiosis types (mutualism, commensalism, parasitism) — lichens are the textbook mutualism example.

questions.stem: The body of a multicellular fungus is composed of branched threads called:
questions.explanation: FUNGAL ANATOMY: a single thread is a HYPHA (plural: hyphae). The mass of intertwined hyphae is the MYCELIUM — the actual 'body' of the fungus. The visible MUSHROOM is just the FRUITING BODY (basidiocarp) — sex organ for spore release; most of the fungus lives unseen in soil/wood. SEPTATE vs ASEPTATE HYPHAE: septate (with cross-walls) — Ascomycetes (Penicillium); aseptate/coenocytic (multinucleate, no walls) — Zygomycetes (Rhizopus). LARGEST ORGANISM: Armillaria ostoyae (honey fungus) in Oregon's Malheur National Forest covers ~9.6 km² of mycelium underground — by area, the largest single organism on Earth, ~2400-8000 years old. SCIENCE: hyphae secrete digestive enzymes externally onto food (extracellular digestion), then absorb nutrients — opposite of human digestion. MYCORRHIZAE: hyphae extend plant root systems by 100-1000× — boosting water and phosphorus uptake; ~90% of plants depend on this fungal partnership. PYQ FREQUENCY: NCERT Class 11 vocabulary; 1-2 such Qs per NEET cycle.

questions.stem: Mushrooms (edible and poisonous) belong to which fungal class based on their characteristic spore-bearing structure?
questions.explanation: FUNGAL CLASSES — based on sexual spore-bearing structures: (1) ZYGOMYCETES — produce zygospores; e.g., Rhizopus (bread mould). (2) ASCOMYCETES — produce ascospores in a sac (ascus); e.g., Saccharomyces (yeast), Penicillium, Aspergillus, morels, truffles. (3) BASIDIOMYCETES — produce basidiospores on club-shaped basidia; e.g., MUSHROOMS, toadstools, smuts, rusts (cereal-crop pathogens). (4) DEUTEROMYCETES — 'imperfect fungi'; sexual stage unknown. EDIBLE MUSHROOMS: button (Agaricus bisporus), oyster (Pleurotus), shiitake (Lentinula edodes), portobello, enoki. POISONOUS: Amanita phalloides (death cap — kills 50% of victims), Amanita muscaria (psychoactive). INDIA: Dehradun has ICAR's Directorate of Mushroom Research; India produces ~200,000 tonnes/year — a growing rural micro-enterprise. PYQ ANGLE: NEET, NCERT-driven SSC questions test the four-class fungal taxonomy regularly. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests systematic biology + spore terminology — solid Class 11 syllabus content.
